subject: Problems installing packages in R Studio 3.1.2

messages.author: 9c1a93cd557f488e
messages.subject: Problems installing packages in R Studio 3.1.2
parts:
Hi
All of the sudden I am having problems installing any/all packages in R studio.
I get this error message: 
Warning in install.packages :
  unable to access index for repository https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/mavericks/contrib/3.1
Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘MASS’ is not available (for R version 3.1.2)

I have a Mac. Any ideas on why this might be happening? Should I just reinstall the whole program?
Thanks
Laura

messages.author: 2226e6c311219eb7
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Problems installing packages in R Studio 3.1.2
parts:
Hi Laura

Check that you can visit that URL
https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/mavericks/contrib/3.1
in your Web browser.
If not, then you probably have a general network connectivity issue
as I can get a response from the site presently. It may be that it was down
for a while and has returned.

You can also use a different mirror, e.g.,
options(repos = 'https://cran.r-project.org')
and then try installing a package.

D.

messages.author: aee29fb701354d0d
messages.subject: Problems installing packages in R Studio 3.1.2
parts:
R now defaults to secure connections (https) which are prone to throw these errors. Change the repo to http and you're all set.

http://blog.rstudio.org/2015/08/17/secure-https-connections-for-r/

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/206827897-Secure-Package-Downloads-for-R

--
mtb

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Problems installing packages in R Studio 3.1.2
parts:
I've noticed that behavior as well. I've tried numerous times to use
an "https" CRAN mirror as the repository, and it has *never* worked.
Hence, I now always specify the "http" version. If anyone can
enlighten me as the reason for this puzzling behavior (i.e.,
defaulting to https, then always failing), I'd appreciate it.

I might add that I'm not overly concerned about the lack of encryption
while updating, say, rmarkdown. (I know there are those who advocate
for *always* using https, but I don't see that it makes much
difference in my own use case -- using wired Ethernet to connect to a
known CRAN mirror at UCB or UCLA.)

-- Mike
